correctness.rationale: The two apices must match to different rim vertices a,b. The two remaining paths have even orders exactly when a,b have opposite parity; then the matchings of the paths are forced. This proves the facet count 2m² and agrees with the independent uncovered-vertex recursion (18,32,50). The verified complexes are the downward closures of those perfect matchings, not all ordinary matchings. In the independent reduction, each pair was a live codimension-one face with unique immediate coface, hence a free face in the current simplicial complex. The different valid reduction orders in source and replay need not give the same core. The replay's six-rim core is a connected graph with (11,14) vertices and edges and cycle rank 4. The eight-rim (15,50,39) and ten-rim (17,69,91,39) cores each admit a spanning tree and triangle closure on all other edges (36 and 53 respectively); the two known edges in each chosen triangle express the unknown generator, and induction makes all surviving generators trivial. The eight-rim simply connected 2-complex has H_2 free of rank 3 by χ=4 and is a wedge by Hurewicz and Whitehead. In the ten-rim replay ∂_3 has rank 37 with all nonzero Smith factors 1; the source's different core uses a unit rank-eight minor and two independent kernel vectors. Either computation proves primitivity, giving integral H_2=Z and H_3=Z². For homotopy recognition, the 2-skeleton of either simply connected 3-core is simply connected and equivalent to a wedge of 2-spheres, as follows by Hurewicz and Whitehead. The 3-cell attaching maps are classified by their degrees on that wedge. Their image is primitive in H_2 of the 2-skeleton, since it is primitive even in C_2. The integral degree matrix can be brought to a block of ones and zeros by changes of bases of target and source wedges, realized by homotopy equivalences (again by Hurewicz and Whitehead). The homotopy cofiber then retains one S² and two S³. The known B_4 octahedral perfect-matching complex is a wedge of five circles, so the decagonal case is indeed the first mix within the stated consecutive sizes.
residual_risks: Proof is finite for m=3,4,5; no extrapolation. Independent replay used 79,258,832 alternate free-face pairs and did not duplicate the frozen order.

evidence: Their inspected scopes are respectively open three-row grids, cubic Möbius/circular ladders, linearly joined polygons (with an even-polygon contractibility theorem), and honeycomb families.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These graph families do not instantiate a 2m-cycle whose entire rim sees two nonadjacent apices. In particular the apices have degree 2m, excluding cubic ladders and honeycomb graphs, and the even-polygon line-tiling result requires a different construction.

value.rationale: The first small even bipyramids are a natural sequence beginning at the octahedron, and the decagonal row is a concrete first mixed-dimensional boundary within it. The extendibility restriction changes the topology significantly from the already studied ordinary octagonal complex. The exact integral types and location of the first mixed case within the stated consecutive range are useful comparison data, not a generic extrapolation or an isolated collapse count. The cap at ten is justified by reaching that boundary.
residual_risks: No claim beyond the ten-rim case or for graphs with an apex-to-apex edge.
